1.title: Shared Responsibility, Governance and Compliance
1.text: Welcome to Module three: Shared Responsibility, Governance and Compliance. This module opens the second domain of the exam, Security and Compliance, which is thirty percent of scored content. It covers task statements two point one and two point two: the shared responsibility model, and the security, governance and compliance concepts around it.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Explain the shared responsibility model: security of the cloud, and security in the cloud. Say how responsibility shifts between Amazon E C two, Amazon R D S and A W S Lambda. Find compliance reports and agreements with A W S Artifact. Describe encryption in transit and at rest, A W S K M S, and A W S Certificate Manager. And tell CloudTrail, CloudWatch, A W S Config and Control Tower apart, and know where logs live.

1.title: Case Check-In: Tidewater Asks Who Secures What
1.text: Tidewater's founder asks a fair question: if we run on A W S, isn't A W S responsible for our security? The shop will use virtual servers, a managed database and serverless functions. An auditor wants proof of A W S's own compliance reports. And the team wants to know who changed a setting, and whether resources follow its rules. Your job is to draw the line between A W S's duties and Tidewater's, and to pick the governance tools.

1.title: Security of the Cloud, Security in the Cloud
1.text: Security on A W S is a shared responsibility. Look at the two bands. The lower band is security of the cloud: A W S protects the infrastructure that runs all A W S services. The upper band is security in the cloud, and that is the customer's part, which depends on the services the customer chooses. Customers are also responsible for the sensitivity of their data, and for the laws that apply to them. Exam tip: of the cloud is A W S, and in the cloud is you.

1.title: What AWS Is Responsible For
1.text: What does A W S take care of? It protects the hardware, software, networking and facilities that run its services. That runs from the host operating system and the virtualization layer down to the physical security of the data centers. A W S provides services you can use securely, and independent auditors test its controls. A W S also patches its own infrastructure, and trains its own employees. Exam tip: data center security, hardware and the virtualization layer are always A W S's responsibility.

1.title: What You Are Responsible For
1.text: Now the customer's side. It typically includes the guest operating system and its patches, the applications you install, and the security group firewall configuration. It includes your data: how it is managed, classified and encrypted. And it includes identity and access: who can do what, set with I A M, which Module four covers. The more abstracted the service, the less you configure, but your data and access stay yours. Your duties are set by the services you select. Exam tip: data, access and the configuration of what you deploy are always yours.

1.title: Inherited, Shared and Customer-Specific Controls
1.text: A W S describes three kinds of controls. Inherited controls you fully inherit from A W S, such as physical and environmental controls. Shared controls apply to both sides, each in its own context: patch management, configuration management, and awareness and training. A W S patches its infrastructure and you patch what you run; A W S configures its devices and you configure your systems; A W S trains its staff and you train yours. Customer-specific controls are yours alone, set by your application, such as routing data within security zones. Exam tip: the shared controls to remember are patching, configuration and training.

1.title: Responsibility Shifts With the Service
1.text: Responsibility is not fixed: it shifts with the service. Look at the three columns. On Amazon E C two, you manage the guest operating system, your software and your security groups. On Amazon R D S, A W S also manages operating system and database patching, backups and failover. On A W S Lambda, A W S manages the servers, patching, capacity and scaling. In every column, the data and access layer stays with the customer. A managed service moves work to A W S, but it never removes your data and access duties. Exam tip: from E C two to R D S to Lambda, A W S takes on more of the stack.

1.title: Amazon EC2: Most of the Management Is Yours
1.text: Amazon E C two is infrastructure as a service, so the customer handles nearly all security configuration and management of the instance. You apply guest operating system updates and security patches. You manage the software and utilities you install, and the security group firewall. A W S manages the hardware layers, so you do not run server hardware. Be aware that updating an operating system or a database by hand can cause user errors and downtime. Exam tip: patching the operating system of an E C two instance is your job, not A W S's.

1.title: Amazon RDS: AWS Runs the Database Platform
1.text: Amazon R D S shows the shift clearly. A W S compares four ways of running a database. Application optimization is the customer's job in all three. For database software and operating system patching, on premises and on E C two it is you, but on R D S it is A W S. The same goes for backups, scaling and high availability. For server maintenance, hardware and power, on premises it is you, but on E C two and R D S it is A W S. You still tune queries, and control access with I A M and V P C security groups. Exam tip: on R D S, A W S patches the engine and the O S, and you tune the queries and control access.

1.title: AWS Lambda and Other Abstracted Services
1.text: A W S Lambda runs your code without you provisioning or managing servers. A W S manages server maintenance, capacity, scaling and patching. You provide the code, its permissions and your data. Amazon S three and Dynamo D B are abstracted services too: A W S operates the infrastructure, the operating system and the platform. You use endpoints to store data, and you manage your data, your encryption options, how data is classified, and the I A M permissions. Your duties also follow your data and the laws that apply to it. Exam tip: on abstracted services you give up servers, not responsibility for data and access.

1.title: Who Is Responsible?
1.text: Let us practice. Physical security of the data center is A W S. The hypervisor and host operating system are A W S. Patching the guest operating system on an E C two instance is the customer. Patching the database engine on Amazon R D S is A W S. Setting a security group rule is the customer. And deciding who may read an S three bucket is the customer. Exam tip: ask two questions. Is it infrastructure that A W S runs, and which service is it on?

1.title: Common Traps: Shared Responsibility
1.text: Watch for five traps. A W S is responsible for my data is wrong: you classify, protect and control access to your data. A managed service means no security work is wrong too: access, data and settings remain yours. Patching is shared, not one-sided: A W S patches its infrastructure, and you patch what you run. Responsibility is not fixed, because it shifts with the service. And compliance is shared as well: A W S has certifications, and you follow your own laws. Exam tip: a statement that says A W S handles everything, or that you handle everything, is usually wrong.

2.title: AWS Compliance Programs and Your Part
2.text: A W S compliance programs help customers understand the controls in place at A W S. They fall into three groups: certifications and attestations, laws, regulations and privacy, and alignments and frameworks. Examples include I S O two seven zero zero one, S O C one, two and three, and P C I D S S, which are global; H I P A A in the United States; and G D P R in Europe. Independent auditors assess many of them. But you remain responsible for complying with the laws and rules that apply to your business. Exam tip: A W S's certifications cover A W S's side, and your compliance is still your job.

2.title: AWS Artifact: Reports and Agreements
2.text: A W S Artifact gives on-demand downloads of A W S security and compliance documents. Look at the picture. There are two kinds. Reports include I S O, P C I and S O C reports, and certifications from accreditation bodies. Agreements let you review, accept and track your agreements with A W S, for one account or for many accounts in an organization. You can give the documents to auditors or regulators as audit artifacts. Documents and agreements are free of charge, but you still produce your own evidence. Exam tip: where do I find A W S's compliance reports? A W S Artifact.

2.title: Compliance Varies by Location, Industry and Service
2.text: Compliance needs differ by country and industry. H I P A A applies to health data in the United States, G D P R to personal data in Europe, and P C I D S S to payment cards. A W S publishes a list called A W S Services in Scope by Compliance Program, and not every service is in scope for every program. Generally available features are considered in scope unless excluded, and a service missing from a list is not forbidden. You decide how a service affects your compliance, based on your data. Exam tip: before relying on a service for regulated data, check it is in scope for the program you need.

2.title: Encryption: In Transit and At Rest
2.text: Encryption comes in two forms. Encryption in transit protects data as it travels, using S S L or T L S. Encryption at rest protects stored data. It can be server-side, done by the service, or client-side, done by you before you upload. Amazon S three encrypts every new object at rest by default with S S E dash S three, since the fifth of January, twenty twenty-three. You can choose S S E dash K M S, D S S E dash K M S, or S S E dash C. With client-side encryption, you manage the process and the keys. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, check the S three documentation for current defaults. Exam tip: moving across a network is in transit; sitting on a disk or in a bucket is at rest.

2.title: AWS KMS and AWS Certificate Manager
2.text: Two services support encryption. A W S Key Management Service, K M S, creates and controls the keys that encrypt and sign your data. K M S keys are protected by hardware security modules and never leave K M S unencrypted, and key policies control who may use them. A W S Certificate Manager, A C M, creates, stores and renews S S L and T L S certificates for A W S websites and applications. Certificates managed with A C M carry no additional charge; you pay for the resources you run. K M S serves encryption at rest, and A C M serves encryption in transit. Exam tip: encryption keys, K M S. T L S certificates, A C M.

2.title: Where to Find Logs
2.text: The exam guide asks where to capture and locate logs. Look at the three sources. A W S CloudTrail records account activity, meaning A P I calls, where A P I stands for application programming interface: who did what, and when, and trails deliver events to an Amazon S three bucket. Amazon CloudWatch Logs collects logs from A W S services and from your applications. And V P C Flow Logs capture I P traffic to and from network interfaces, and publish to CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S three, or Amazon Data Firehose. Exam tip: A P I activity, CloudTrail. Network traffic, V P C Flow Logs. Service and application logs, CloudWatch Logs.

2.title: AWS CloudTrail: Who Did What, and When
2.text: A W S CloudTrail supports auditing, governance and compliance. It records the actions of a user, a role or an A W S service as events, including actions from the console, the command line interface, or C L I, software development kits, or S D Ks, and A P Is. Event history is a viewable, searchable record of the past ninety days of management events in a Region, with no CloudTrail charge to view. Trails and CloudTrail Lake keep events for longer. In short, it shows who acted, on what, and when. Exam tip: who deleted that resource, and when? CloudTrail.

2.title: Amazon CloudWatch: Metrics, Logs and Alarms
2.text: Amazon CloudWatch monitors A W S resources and applications in real time. Metrics track performance data, dashboards show it in one place, and alarms watch metrics against thresholds. Alarms can notify you, and they can trigger automated actions. CloudWatch Logs collects, stores and queries logs. And many A W S services send basic metrics for free. Exam tip: is it healthy right now, and who should be told if not? CloudWatch.

2.title: AWS Config: What Changed, and Is It Compliant?
2.text: A W S Config gives a detailed view of resource configuration, how resources relate, and how they changed over time. Config rules check settings and flag noncompliant resources, and conformance packs bundle rules together. Aggregators give one view across accounts and Regions. It is useful for auditing, for security analysis, and for finding the last known good configuration. Exam tip: what changed, and does it meet our rules? A W S Config.

2.title: CloudTrail, CloudWatch or Config?
2.text: These three services are easy to mix up. Which user called which A P I, and when? CloudTrail. Is C P U high right now, and alert me? CloudWatch. How was this security group set last month? A W S Config. Does this resource break our rules? A W S Config. And keep a record of account activity for auditors? CloudTrail. Exam tip: activity is CloudTrail, health is CloudWatch, and configuration is Config.

2.title: AWS Control Tower: Governing Many Accounts
2.text: A W S Control Tower sets up and governs a multi-account environment, following best practices. It builds a landing zone, orchestrating A W S Organizations, Service Catalog and I A M Identity Center. Controls, also called guardrails, are high-level rules: preventive, detective or proactive. Account Factory provisions new accounts from approved templates. And a dashboard shows accounts, controls and noncompliant resources. Exam tip: to set up and govern many accounts the same way, think A W S Control Tower.

2.title: Access Reports and Security Services
2.text: A few more tools appear in task statement two point two. The I A M credential report lists users and the state of their passwords, access keys and M F A, or multi-factor authentication, devices, as a C S V, or comma-separated values, file, up to every four hours. Amazon GuardDuty detects threats from sources such as CloudTrail events, V P C flow logs and D N S, or Domain Name System, logs. Amazon Inspector scans E C two instances, container images and Lambda functions for vulnerabilities. A W S Security Hub collects findings and checks standards; the documentation now calls it Security Hub C S P M. And A W S Shield Standard protects against D D O S, or distributed denial of service, attacks at no extra charge. Module five covers these. Exam tip: detect threats, GuardDuty. Scan for vulnerabilities, Inspector.

2.title: What the Exam Asks: Responsibility and Governance
2.text: Here are the look-alike pairs for this module. Of the cloud or in the cloud: A W S's infrastructure, or your configuration and data. Inherited, shared or customer-specific: all from A W S, both sides, or yours alone. CloudTrail, CloudWatch or Config: who did it, how healthy, or what changed. K M S or A C M: keys for data, or certificates for websites. Artifact or Config: A W S's reports, or your own resource history. And E C two, R D S or Lambda: how much A W S manages for you. Exam tip: name the situation first.

2.title: Design Check: Tidewater's Security Plan
2.text: Time to design. Look at Tidewater's six needs, and answer each one yourself before I do. To understand who secures what, use shared responsibility: A W S of the cloud, Tidewater in the cloud. To prove A W S's compliance to the auditor, download A W S Artifact reports. To find who deleted a security group, use CloudTrail. To alert on high C P U, use a CloudWatch alarm. To check settings against its rules, use A W S Config rules. And to encrypt customer data at rest, use A W S K M S keys.

3.title: Module Recap
3.text: Let us recap. A W S secures the cloud, you secure what you put in it, and responsibility shifts with the service. Controls are inherited from A W S, shared, such as patching, configuration and training, or customer-specific. E C two is mostly yours, R D S has A W S manage the platform, and Lambda has A W S manage the servers. A W S Artifact provides A W S's reports and agreements, and compliance varies by location, industry and service. Encryption uses T L S in transit, and server-side or client-side encryption at rest, with K M S for keys and A C M for certificates. And for governance: CloudTrail for activity, CloudWatch for health, Config for configuration, and Control Tower for many accounts.

3.title: Practice Question 1
3.text: Question one. Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for the physical security of A W S data centers? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B, A W S, as part of security of the cloud. Customers inherit these controls and do not manage the data centers themselves.

3.title: Practice Question 2
3.text: Question two. Which task is the customer's responsibility for an Amazon E C two instance? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D, applying security patches to the guest operating system. A W S handles the hardware, the virtualization layer and the facility.

3.title: Practice Question 3
3.text: Question three. Select two. Tidewater runs its database on Amazon R D S. Which two tasks does A W S handle? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C: patching the database engine software, and patching the operating system of the database host. Query tuning, access control and the choice of data remain the customer's responsibility.

3.title: Practice Question 4
3.text: Question four. Tidewater moves a function to A W S Lambda. Which task stays with Tidewater? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A, writing and securing the function code and its permissions. Lambda manages servers, capacity, scaling and patching.

3.title: Practice Question 5
3.text: Question five. Which term describes controls that a customer fully inherits from A W S, such as physical and environmental controls? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C, inherited controls. Shared controls apply to both sides, and customer-specific controls are solely the customer's.

3.title: Practice Question 6
3.text: Question six. Which is an example of a shared control? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B, patch management. A W S patches its infrastructure, and the customer patches what it runs. Physical access and hardware lifecycle are A W S's, and security zone routing is customer-specific.

3.title: Practice Question 7
3.text: Question seven. Tidewater stores customer photos in Amazon S three. Which responsibility belongs to Tidewater? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C, choosing who may access the photos and which encryption options to use. On an abstracted service such as S three, A W S runs the infrastructure and platform.

3.title: Practice Question 8
3.text: Question eight. Select two. Which two describe A W S Artifact? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C: it provides on-demand downloads of compliance reports, and lets you review and accept agreements with A W S. CloudTrail records A P I calls, GuardDuty detects threats, and K M S manages keys.

3.title: Practice Question 9
3.text: Question nine. Tidewater's auditor asks for A W S's S O C report. Where can Tidewater download it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A, A W S Artifact. It provides on-demand downloads of A W S compliance reports such as S O C, I S O and P C I.

3.title: Practice Question 10
3.text: Question ten. Tidewater needs to learn which user deleted a security group yesterday. Which service records this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C, A W S CloudTrail. It records account activity, showing who took which action and when.

3.title: Practice Question 11
3.text: Question eleven. Which service records how a resource was configured in the past and flags settings that break your rules? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B, A W S Config. It keeps resource configuration history and evaluates it against rules.

3.title: Practice Question 12
3.text: Question twelve. Which statement about A W S K M S is correct? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: it creates and controls the keys used to encrypt and sign data. Certificates are managed by A W S Certificate Manager, and A P I activity by CloudTrail.

3.title: Practice Question 13
3.text: Question thirteen. Select two. Tidewater wants customer data protected in transit and at rest. Which two actions fit? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C: T L S for connections, and encryption with K M S keys for stored data. Turning off logging, sharing the root password, and storing plain text all weaken security.

3.title: Practice Question 14
3.text: Question fourteen. Tidewater is adding many A W S accounts and wants standard account setup with guardrails. Which service helps? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A, A W S Control Tower. It sets up and governs a multi-account environment with controls and Account Factory.

3.title: Answers at a Glance
3.text: Here are all fourteen answers. Question one: B. Question two: D. Question three: A and C. Question four: A. Question five: C. Question six: B. Question seven: C. Question eight: A and C. Question nine: A. Question ten: C. Question eleven: B. Question twelve: D. Question thirteen: A and C. Question fourteen: A. That completes Module three. Next, Module four covers identity and access management.
